rationale:
Split into 6 children: five new leaf lemmas (prefix dtc_bc_lc_sl_sf_) and one reused accepted declaration, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, with its identical frozen type.

Why split. The supplied proof of slice_family (steps 0–9) is long. Apart from building the slices and the final bookkeeping, it rests on five general facts that do not depend on the particular T and f:
(i) multilinear algebra of unit orientations (steps 0(a), 3(a), 3(c); Simon 4.3);
(ii) the chain rule for the approximate tangential gradient of the cut-off γ_{a,b}∘f (step 9(a); Simon's (4));
(iii) consequences of the co-area identity: a.e. properties pass to a.e. slices, G vanishes a.e. on level sets, and slices are locally finite (steps 2(a), 2(b), 4; Simon 4.1–4.2);
(iv) the co-area formula for signed integrands (steps 8, 9(c));
(v) a Borel subset of a rectifiable set, oriented by tangent planes of the bigger set, is an IMRep (step 5(a); Simon 4.4, via TL).
Each is stated generally with explicit hypotheses. The co-area children take the identity (CF), and cutoff_gradient takes the approximate differentiability (A), exactly in the form output by sibling coarea. So no child depends on the still-decomposing siblings coarea or lipschitz_leibniz. This node is at depth 5 (max 6), so the children are leaves; each was proved in Lean to confirm it is a provable leaf.

What remains for this node, using coarea, lipschitz_leibniz and the children:
- a Borel version ξ₀ of ξ;
- ζ := ξ₀(ν♭∧·) with ν = G/|G| on {G ≠ 0}, and 0 elsewhere;
- the set of good levels and R_t (the empty triple for bad t);
- the bookkeeping for (1)–(4).

Children (supplied-proof step → child):

4. coarea_signed: 8, 9(c).
5. im_calculus (reuse): TL, used by 6.

Dependencies are acyclic: only 6 ← 5.

subproblems.title: Unit orientations: operator-norm bound and the interior product ξ⌞ν orienting Q ∩ ν^⊥ (Simon Ch. 6, 4.3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Write Λ^k := Covector (Euclid P) k for the continuous alternating k-forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm ‖·‖, and MultiVector P k := (Λ^k →L[ℝ] ℝ). Call ξ ∈ MultiVector P k a unit orientation of a linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P (contract IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q) if there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_k) in ℝ^P with span τ = Q such that ξ(α) = α(τ) for every α ∈ Λ^k, or ξ(α) = −α(τ) for every α ∈ Λ^k. (a) If ξ ∈ MultiVector P n is a unit orientation of Q, then |ξ(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every α ∈ Λ^n. (b) Let ξ ∈ MultiVector P (n+1) be a unit orientation of Q, let v ∈ Q with v ≠ 0, put ν := |v|⁻¹v, and let ζ ∈ MultiVector P n satisfy ζ(α) = ξ(ν♭ ∧ α) for every α ∈ Λ^n, where ν♭ := ⟨ν, ·⟩ (innerSL ℝ ν) and ν♭ ∧ α := alternatizeUncurryFin(ν♭.smulRight α), i.e. (ν♭ ∧ α)(w_0, …, w_n) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i ⟨ν, w_i⟩ α(w_0, …, ŵ_i, …, w_n). Then ζ is a unit orientation of Q ⊓ (span{v})^⊥ = Q ∩ v^⊥. This is Simon's claim in 4.3 that ξ⌞ν, defined by ⟨ξ⌞ν, α⟩ = ⟨ξ, ν ∧ α⟩, is a unit simple n-vector orienting T_xM ∩ ν^⊥ when ξ orients T_xM and ν ∈ T_xM is a unit vector.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (ξ : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ α| ≤ ‖α‖) ∧ ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ξ : MultiVector P (n + 1)) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (v : Euclid P) (ζ : MultiVector P n), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → v ∈ Q → v ≠ 0 → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ζ α = ξ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (‖v‖⁻¹ • v)).smulRight α))) → IsUnitOrientationOf ζ (Q ⊓ (ℝ ∙ v)ᗮ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the supplied proof of the parent node slice_family, steps 0(a), 3(a) and 3(c). Simon Ch. 6, 4.3 (book/chapter-06.txt ll. 1208–1218, printed p. 155) states the conclusion of (b) without proof ("is simple ∈ Λ_{n−1}(T_xM_t) ⊂ Λ_{n−1}(T_xM) and has unit length", with ⟨v⌞w, a⟩ = ⟨v, w ∧ a⟩). The argument below is the one written out in the supplied proof, with the details filled in. For a family w = (w_1, …, w_k) of vectors, α(w) denotes the value of the k-covector α at w.

Part (a).
1. By the definition of IsUnitOrientationOf there is τ : Fin n → ℝ^P, orthonormal, with span τ = Q, and either ξ(α) = α(τ) for all α ∈ Λ^n or ξ(α) = −α(τ) for all α ∈ Λ^n. In both cases |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)|.
2. By the operator-norm inequality for continuous alternating maps (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ · ∏_{i} |τ_i|.
3. Each |τ_i| = 1 because τ is orthonormal, so the product equals 1 (it is the empty product 1 when n = 0). Hence |ξ(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every α ∈ Λ^n.

Part (b).
4. Dimension of Q. By the definition of IsUnitOrientationOf there are τ : Fin (n+1) → ℝ^P, orthonormal, with span τ = Q, and a sign s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(β) = s·β(τ) for every β ∈ Λ^{n+1}. An orthonormal family is linearly independent, so τ is a basis of Q and dim Q = n + 1. In particular τ is an orthonormal basis of Q.
5. The unit vector ν. Since v ≠ 0, |v| > 0 and ν := |v|⁻¹v satisfies |ν| = 1. Since Q is a subspace and v ∈ Q, ν ∈ Q. Moreover span{ν} = span{v} (ν is a nonzero multiple of v), so v^⊥ = ν^⊥.
6. Dimension of Q'. Put Q' := Q ⊓ (span{v})^⊥. Since span{v} ⊆ Q, Q is the orthogonal direct sum of span{v} and Q', so dim span{v} + dim Q' = dim Q (Mathlib Submodule.finrank_add_inf_finrank_orthogonal). As dim span{v} = 1, dim Q' = n.
7. Choose an orthonormal basis τ' = (τ'_1, …, τ'_n) of Q', indexed by Fin n. For instance, take stdOrthonormalBasis of Q' and reindex it along dim Q' = n with finCongr. Orthonormality transfers to ℝ^P along the isometric inclusion (Q'.subtypeₗᵢ.orthonormal_comp_iff). Viewed in ℝ^P, τ' is orthonormal, span τ' = Q', each τ'_j ∈ Q, and ⟨ν, τ'_j⟩ = 0 because τ'_j ⊥ v and ν is a multiple of v.
8. The basis σ. Let σ := (ν, τ'_1, …, τ'_n) = Fin.cons ν τ' : Fin (n+1) → ℝ^P. It is orthonormal (|ν| = 1, τ' orthonormal, ⟨ν, τ'_j⟩ = 0), all its vectors lie in Q, and it has n + 1 = dim Q vectors. Being linearly independent, σ is an orthonormal basis of Q. (In Lean: OrthonormalBasis.mk, with ⊤ ≤ span obtained from basisOfOrthonormalOfCardEqFinrank; evaluate its vectors with OrthonormalBasis.coe_mk.)
9. Uniform sign. Let β ∈ Λ^{n+1}. Its restriction β_Q to Q is β composed with the inclusion Q → ℝ^P in each slot (β.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap Q.subtype). It is an alternating (n+1)-form on the (n+1)-dimensional space Q. Hence β_Q = β_Q(σ) · det_σ, where det_σ is the determinant with respect to the basis σ (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at the basis τ of Q gives β(τ) = det_σ(τ) · β(σ). Since σ and τ are orthonormal bases of the same real inner product space Q, det_σ(τ) ∈ {1, −1} (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real). Put ε := s · det_σ(τ) ∈ {1, −1}. It does not depend on β, and ξ(β) = s·β(τ) = ε·β(σ) for every β ∈ Λ^{n+1}.
10. Expansion of the wedge. Let α ∈ Λ^n. By the formula for alternatizeUncurryFin (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply), (ν♭ ∧ α)(σ) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i ⟨ν, σ_i⟩ α(σ_0, …, σ̂_i, …, σ_n), where the hat means omission (Fin.removeNth). For i = 0 the term is ⟨ν, ν⟩ α(τ') = α(τ'), because |ν| = 1 and removing the 0-th entry of Fin.cons ν τ' leaves τ'. For 1 ≤ i ≤ n, σ_i = τ'_i and ⟨ν, τ'_i⟩ = 0, so the term vanishes. Hence (ν♭ ∧ α)(σ) = α(τ').
11. Consequently, for every α ∈ Λ^n, ζ(α) = ξ(ν♭ ∧ α) = ε·(ν♭ ∧ α)(σ) = ε·α(τ'). This uses the hypothesis on ζ, step 9 with β := ν♭ ∧ α, and step 10.
12. Conclusion. τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P is orthonormal with span τ' = Q' = Q ⊓ (span{v})^⊥. Either ζ(α) = α(τ') for all α (if ε = 1) or ζ(α) = −α(τ') for all α (if ε = −1). This is exactly IsUnitOrientationOf ζ (Q ⊓ (span{v})^⊥). When n = 0 the same argument applies: τ' is the empty family, Q' = 0 = span ∅, σ = (ν), and α(τ') is the value of the 0-covector α. ∎
proof_key_steps: (a) ξ(α) = ±α(τ) with τ orthonormal, and |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏|τ_i| = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
(b) dim Q = n+1. ν := |v|⁻¹v ∈ Q is a unit vector, and Q' := Q ⊓ span{v}^⊥ has dimension n. Take an orthonormal basis τ' of Q'; then σ := Fin.cons ν τ' is an orthonormal basis of Q.
Uniform sign: on Q, β = β(σ)·det_σ (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det) and det_σ(τ) = ±1 for orthonormal bases, so ξ(β) = εβ(σ) for one ε ∈ {±1}.
alternatizeUncurryFin expansion: (ν♭∧α)(ν, τ') = ⟨ν,ν⟩α(τ') + Σ_{i≥1}(−1)^i⟨ν,τ'_i⟩(…) = α(τ').
Hence ζ(α) = εα(τ') for all α, i.e. ζ is a unit orientation of Q ⊓ span{v}^⊥.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangential gradient of the cut-off γ_{a,b}∘f (Simon Ch. 6, chain rule (4) in the proof of 4.5(2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, N ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, and real numbers a < b. Write H^N := μHE[N], T_xM := approxTangentPlane N M x, γ(s) := min{1, max{0, (b − s)/(b − a)}}, h := γ∘f, and H(x) := −(b − a)⁻¹G(x) if a < f(x) < b, H(x) := 0 otherwise. Assume: (i) for H^N-a.e. x ∈ M, M has approximate tangent space T_xM at x, G(x) ∈ T_xM, and for every ε > 0, H^N({y ∈ M ∩ B_r(x) : ε|y − x| < |f(y) − f(x) − ⟨G(x), y − x⟩|})/r^N → 0 as r ↓ 0 (the quotient taken in [0, ∞] with denominator ENNReal.ofReal(r^N)); (ii) G(x) = 0 for H^N-a.e. x ∈ M with f(x) = a; (iii) G(x) = 0 for H^N-a.e. x ∈ M with f(x) = b. Then for H^N-a.e. x ∈ M: M has approximate tangent space T_xM at x, H(x) ∈ T_xM, and for every ε > 0, H^N({y ∈ M ∩ B_r(x) : ε|y − x| < |h(y) − h(x) − ⟨H(x), y − x⟩|})/r^N → 0 as r ↓ 0. In Simon's notation: ∇^M(γ∘f) = γ'(f)∇^M f H^N-a.e. on M, with γ'(f) := 0 at the bad values a, b.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the supplied proof of the parent node slice_family, step 9(a). This is Simon Ch. 6, the chain rule (4) in the proof of 4.5(2) (book/chapter-06.txt ll. 1302–1310, printed pp. 156–157): "∇^M h = γ'(f)∇^M f H^n-a.e. on M (where we set γ'(f) = 0 when f takes the bad values t or t − ε; note that ∇^M h(x) = ∇^M f(x) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x in {x ∈ M : f(x) = c}, c any given constant)", with a = t − ε and b = t.

1. Good points. Each of the following holds for H^N⌞M-a.e. x: the three statements in (i) at x; f(x) = a ⇒ G(x) = 0; f(x) = b ⇒ G(x) = 0. A finite intersection of H^N⌞M-a.e. properties is again H^N⌞M-a.e., so for H^N⌞M-a.e. x all of them hold simultaneously. (M need not be Borel, and membership x ∈ M is never used below.) Fix such an x; we prove the three conclusions at x.
2. Tangent space. By (i), M has approximate tangent space T_xM at x.
3. H(x) ∈ T_xM. If a < f(x) < b, then H(x) = −(b − a)⁻¹G(x) is a scalar multiple of G(x) ∈ T_xM, and T_xM is a linear subspace. Otherwise H(x) = 0 ∈ T_xM.
4. Notation and claim. For δ > 0 and r > 0 put E_f(δ, r) := {y ∈ M ∩ B_r(x) : δ|y − x| < |f(y) − f(x) − ⟨G(x), y − x⟩|} and E_h(ε, r) := {y ∈ M ∩ B_r(x) : ε|y − x| < |h(y) − h(x) − ⟨H(x), y − x⟩|}. Fix ε > 0 and put δ := (b − a)ε > 0. Claim: there is r₁ > 0 such that E_h(ε, r) ⊆ E_f(δ, r) for every 0 < r < r₁.
5. Properties of γ.
 (a) γ is (b − a)⁻¹-Lipschitz on ℝ: s ↦ (b − s)/(b − a) is (b − a)⁻¹-Lipschitz, and u ↦ max{0, u} and u ↦ min{1, u} are 1-Lipschitz.
 (b) If a < s < b, then 0 < (b − s)/(b − a) < 1, so γ(s) = (b − s)/(b − a).
 (c) If s < a, then (b − s)/(b − a) > 1, so γ(s) = 1.
 (d) If s > b, then (b − s)/(b − a) < 0, so γ(s) = 0.
6. Case a < f(x) < b. Since f is continuous and (a, b) is open, there is r₁ > 0 with a < f(y) < b for all y ∈ B_{r₁}(x). For such y, by 5(b) and H(x) = −(b − a)⁻¹G(x): h(y) − h(x) − ⟨H(x), y − x⟩ = (b − f(y))/(b − a) − (b − f(x))/(b − a) + (b − a)⁻¹⟨G(x), y − x⟩ = −(b − a)⁻¹[f(y) − f(x) − ⟨G(x), y − x⟩]. Multiplying by b − a > 0, for y ∈ B_{r₁}(x) we get: ε|y − x| < |h(y) − h(x) − ⟨H(x), y − x⟩| if and only if δ|y − x| < |f(y) − f(x) − ⟨G(x), y − x⟩|. Hence E_h(ε, r) = E_f(δ, r) for 0 < r ≤ r₁.
7. Case f(x) < a. By continuity there is r₁ > 0 with f(y) < a for all y ∈ B_{r₁}(x). By 5(c), h(y) = 1 = h(x) for such y, and H(x) = 0 since a < f(x) fails. So h(y) − h(x) − ⟨H(x), y − x⟩ = 0, and ε|y − x| < 0 is false. Hence E_h(ε, r) = ∅ ⊆ E_f(δ, r) for 0 < r ≤ r₁.
8. Case f(x) > b. By continuity there is r₁ > 0 with f(y) > b for all y ∈ B_{r₁}(x). By 5(d), h(y) = 0 = h(x) for such y, and H(x) = 0. As in step 7, E_h(ε, r) = ∅ ⊆ E_f(δ, r) for 0 < r ≤ r₁.
9. Case f(x) = a or f(x) = b. By the choice of x in step 1, G(x) = 0, and H(x) = 0 because a < f(x) < b fails. By 5(a), for every y: |h(y) − h(x) − ⟨H(x), y − x⟩| = |γ(f(y)) − γ(f(x))| ≤ (b − a)⁻¹|f(y) − f(x)| = (b − a)⁻¹|f(y) − f(x) − ⟨G(x), y − x⟩|. So ε|y − x| < |h(y) − h(x) − ⟨H(x), y − x⟩| implies δ|y − x| < |f(y) − f(x) − ⟨G(x), y − x⟩|. Hence E_h(ε, r) ⊆ E_f(δ, r) for every r > 0; take r₁ := 1.
10. The four cases exhaust all possibilities for f(x), which proves the claim of step 4.
11. Limit. For 0 < r < r₁, monotonicity of H^N gives H^N(E_h(ε, r)) ≤ H^N(E_f(δ, r)). Dividing both sides in [0, ∞] by the same ENNReal.ofReal(r^N) gives H^N(E_h(ε, r))/r^N ≤ H^N(E_f(δ, r))/r^N. By (i) applied with δ > 0 in place of ε, the right side tends to 0 as r ↓ 0. The left side is ≥ 0, and the inequality holds for all r in (0, r₁), i.e. eventually along r ↓ 0 (the filter 𝓝[>] 0). By the squeeze theorem, H^N(E_h(ε, r))/r^N → 0 as r ↓ 0. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, the third conclusion holds at x. Together with steps 1–3 this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Restrict to the H^N⌞M-a.e. set of x where (i) holds and G(x) = 0 whenever f(x) ∈ {a, b}.
T_xM exists by (i); H(x) is either a multiple of G(x) ∈ T_xM or 0, so H(x) ∈ T_xM.

With δ := (b−a)ε, show E_h(ε,r) ⊆ E_f(δ,r) for small r in four cases. On {a<f<b} near x: h(y)−h(x)−⟨H(x),y−x⟩ = −(b−a)⁻¹[f(y)−f(x)−⟨G(x),y−x⟩]. Near {f<a} or {f>b}: h is locally constant and H(x)=0. At f(x) ∈ {a,b}: G(x)=H(x)=0 and γ is (b−a)⁻¹-Lipschitz.
Monotonicity of H^N and the squeeze theorem along r ↓ 0 give H^N(E_h(ε,r))/r^N → 0.

subproblems.title: Null sets, level sets and local finiteness of slices from the co-area identity (Simon Ch. 6, 4.1–4.2 with special g)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P Borel, f : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel and G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Borel. Write Hᵏ := μHE[k] and assume the co-area identity (CF): for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], the function t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ is Lebesgue-a.e.-measurable on ℝ and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ dt = ∫_M |G| g dH^{n+1}. Then: (a) (null sets) if a property p holds at H^{n+1}-a.e. point of M, then for L¹-a.e. t it holds at Hⁿ-a.e. point of M ∩ f⁻¹(t); (b) (level sets) for every c ∈ ℝ, G(x) = 0 for H^{n+1}-a.e. x ∈ M with f(x) = c; (c) (local finiteness) if g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] is Borel and ∫_{M∩K} |G| g dH^{n+1} < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, then for L¹-a.e. t, ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)∩K} g dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (G : Euclid P → Euclid P), MeasurableSet M → Measurable f → Measurable G → (∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → AEMeasurable (fun t => ∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂μHE[n]) ∧ ∫⁻ t, ∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂μHE[n] = ∫⁻ x in M, ENNReal.ofReal ‖G x‖ * g x ∂μHE[n + 1]) → (∀ p : Euclid P → Prop, (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n + 1].restrict M), p x) → ∀ᵐ t, ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t})), p x) ∧ (∀ c : ℝ, ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n + 1].restrict M), f x = c → G x = 0) ∧ ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ∫⁻ x in M ∩ K, ENNReal.ofReal ‖G x‖ * g x ∂μHE[n + 1] ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ t, ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t} ∩ K, g x ∂μHE[n] ≠ ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the supplied proof of the parent node slice_family, steps 2(a), 2(b) and the third condition of step 4. These are Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.1, last part (book/chapter-06.txt ll. 1156–1183, printed p. 154), and Remark 4.2 (ll. 1185–1196), used with g an indicator function. This matches Simon's remark in the proof of 4.5(2) that ∇^M f = 0 H^n-a.e. on {x ∈ M : f(x) = c} (ll. 1308–1310). Throughout, S_t := M ∩ f⁻¹(t). S_t is Borel because M is Borel and f is Borel. For a Borel set Z, ∫_{S_t} 1_Z dHⁿ = Hⁿ(Z ∩ S_t).

Part (a).
1. Let Y := {x : p(x) fails}. Since M is Borel, the hypothesis "p holds at H^{n+1}-a.e. point of M" means H^{n+1}(Y ∩ M) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply').
2. Choose a Borel set Z ⊇ Y ∩ M with H^{n+1}(Z) = 0 (Mathlib exists_measurable_superset_of_null).
3. Apply (CF) to the Borel function g := 1_Z. The left side is ∫_ℝ Hⁿ(Z ∩ S_t) dt. On the right side the integrand |G|1_Z vanishes off Z, and H^{n+1}(M ∩ Z) ≤ H^{n+1}(Z) = 0. So the integrand vanishes at H^{n+1}-a.e. point of M and the right side is 0.
4. Hence ∫_ℝ Hⁿ(Z ∩ S_t) dt = 0. By (CF) the integrand t ↦ Hⁿ(Z ∩ S_t) is a.e.-measurable, so it vanishes for L¹-a.e. t (Mathlib lintegral_eq_zero_iff').
5. Fix such a t. Since S_t ⊆ M, Y ∩ S_t ⊆ Y ∩ M ⊆ Z, so Y ∩ S_t ⊆ Z ∩ S_t and Hⁿ(Y ∩ S_t) ≤ Hⁿ(Z ∩ S_t) = 0. As S_t is Borel, this says that p holds at Hⁿ-a.e. point of S_t. This proves (a).

Part (b).
6. Fix c ∈ ℝ and apply (CF) to the Borel function g := 1_{f⁻¹(c)} (Borel since f is Borel). For t ≠ c, S_t ∩ f⁻¹(c) = ∅, so ∫_{S_t} g dHⁿ = Hⁿ(f⁻¹(c) ∩ S_t) = 0. Since L¹({c}) = 0, the integrand of the left side vanishes L¹-a.e., so the left side is 0.
7. Therefore ∫_M |G| 1_{f⁻¹(c)} dH^{n+1} = 0. The integrand x ↦ |G(x)| 1_{f⁻¹(c)}(x) is Borel (G and f are Borel), so it vanishes at H^{n+1}-a.e. x ∈ M (Mathlib lintegral_eq_zero_iff).
8. At such an x with f(x) = c the indicator equals 1, so |G(x)| = 0 and G(x) = 0. This proves (b).

Part (c).
9. For k ∈ ℕ let B_k := closedBall(0, k), a compact Borel subset of ℝ^P (ℝ^P is proper), and g_k := 1_{B_k} g, a Borel function.
10. By (CF), ∫_ℝ ∫_{S_t} g_k dHⁿ dt = ∫_M |G| g_k dH^{n+1} = ∫_{M∩B_k} |G| g dH^{n+1}. This is finite by the hypothesis with K := B_k. The integrand t ↦ ∫_{S_t} g_k dHⁿ = ∫_{S_t∩B_k} g dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable by (CF), so it is finite for L¹-a.e. t (Mathlib ae_lt_top').
11. Since ℕ is countable, for L¹-a.e. t we have ∫_{S_t∩B_k} g dHⁿ < ∞ for all k ∈ ℕ simultaneously (Mathlib ae_all_iff).
12. Fix such a t and a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P. K is bounded, so K ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R ≥ 0, and K ⊆ B_k for any natural number k ≥ R. Then S_t ∩ K ⊆ S_t ∩ B_k. By monotonicity of the integral in the domain, ∫_{S_t∩K} g dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{S_t∩B_k} g dHⁿ < ∞. This proves (c). ∎
proof_key_steps: (a) Enclose the H^{n+1}-null exceptional set of M in a Borel null set Z. (CF) with g = 1_Z gives ∫ Hⁿ(Z ∩ M ∩ f⁻¹(t)) dt = 0, so a.e. slice meets Z in an Hⁿ-null set.
(b) (CF) with g = 1_{f⁻¹(c)}: the slice side vanishes for t ≠ c, so ∫_M |G|1_{f=c} = 0 and G = 0 a.e. on M ∩ {f = c}.
(c) (CF) with g·1_{closedBall(0,k)} gives finiteness of ∫_{slice∩B_k} g for a.e. t. Intersect over k ∈ ℕ and cover each compact K by some B_k.

subproblems.title: Co-area formula for real-valued integrands (Simon Ch. 6, 4.1 applied to q⁺ and q⁻)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P Borel, f : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel and G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Borel. Write Hᵏ := μHE[k] and assume the co-area identity (CF): for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ is Lebesgue-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ dt = ∫_M |G| g dH^{n+1}. Let q : ℝ^P → ℝ be Borel with ∫_M |G||q| dH^{n+1} < ∞. Then (1) for L¹-a.e. t, q is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ f⁻¹(t); (2) t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} q dHⁿ (Bochner integral, which is 0 when q is not integrable on the slice) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ; (3) ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} q dHⁿ dt = ∫_M |G| q dH^{n+1}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (G : Euclid P → Euclid P), MeasurableSet M → Measurable f → Measurable G → (∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → AEMeasurable (fun t => ∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂μHE[n]) ∧ ∫⁻ t, ∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂μHE[n] = ∫⁻ x in M, ENNReal.ofReal ‖G x‖ * g x ∂μHE[n + 1]) → ∀ q : Euclid P → ℝ, Measurable q → ∫⁻ x in M, ENNReal.ofReal ‖G x‖ * ENNReal.ofReal |q x| ∂μHE[n + 1] ≠ ∞ → (∀ᵐ t, IntegrableOn q (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}) μHE[n]) ∧ Integrable (fun t => ∫ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, q x ∂μHE[n]) ∧ ∫ t, ∫ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, q x ∂μHE[n] = ∫ x in M, ‖G x‖ * q x ∂μHE[n + 1]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the supplied proof of the parent node slice_family, steps 8 and 9(c): "Apply (CF) to q⁺ and q⁻ and subtract (all quantities finite)". This is Simon Ch. 6, the last part of Lemma 4.1 (book/chapter-06.txt ll. 1156–1183), applied to the positive and negative parts of the signed integrand. Simon does this in the proof of 4.5(1) (l. 1245) and in "we use 4.2 with g = ⟨ξ⌞∇^M f/|∇^M f|, ω⟩" at the end of the proof of 4.5(2) (ll. 1317–1323).

Notation: S_t := M ∩ f⁻¹(t). For real r, r⁺ := max{r, 0} and r⁻ := max{−r, 0}, so r = r⁺ − r⁻ and |r| = r⁺ + r⁻. Put A⁺(t) := ∫_{S_t} q⁺ dHⁿ, A⁻(t) := ∫_{S_t} q⁻ dHⁿ, A(t) := ∫_{S_t} |q| dHⁿ, with values in [0, ∞] (in Lean the [0, ∞]-valued integrands are ENNReal.ofReal q, ENNReal.ofReal(−q), ENNReal.ofReal|q|). Put F(t) := ∫_{S_t} q dHⁿ (Bochner integral).

1. The functions q⁺, q⁻ and |q| are Borel because q is. By (CF), A⁺, A⁻ and A are a.e.-measurable on ℝ, ∫_ℝ A dt = ∫_M |G||q| dH^{n+1} < ∞, and ∫_ℝ A^± dt = ∫_M |G| q^± dH^{n+1} ≤ ∫_M |G||q| dH^{n+1} < ∞.
2. Since A is a.e.-measurable with finite integral, A(t) < ∞ for L¹-a.e. t (Mathlib ae_lt_top'). For such t, q is Hⁿ-integrable on S_t: it is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable, and ∫_{S_t} |q| dHⁿ = A(t) < ∞. This proves (1). For the same t, A^±(t) ≤ A(t) < ∞.
3. For such t, F(t) = A⁺(t).toReal − A⁻(t).toReal (Mathlib integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part, applied to the integrable function q on S_t). Thus F agrees L¹-a.e. with t ↦ A⁺(t).toReal − A⁻(t).toReal. That function is a.e.-measurable, being a difference of real parts of a.e.-measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions. Hence F is a.e. strongly measurable.
4. For every t, |F(t)| ≤ ∫_{S_t} |q| dHⁿ = A(t). This is the norm bound for Bochner integrals when q is integrable on S_t; otherwise F(t) = 0. Hence ∫_ℝ |F| dt ≤ ∫_ℝ A dt < ∞, and F is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ. This proves (2).
5. The functions t ↦ A^±(t).toReal are nonnegative, a.e.-measurable, and have finite integral (at most ∫_ℝ A^± dt < ∞), so they are integrable. Since A^± < ∞ L¹-a.e., ∫_ℝ A^±(t).toReal dt = (∫_ℝ A^± dt).toReal (Mathlib integral_toReal).
6. By steps 3 and 5, ∫_ℝ F dt = ∫_ℝ A⁺.toReal dt − ∫_ℝ A⁻.toReal dt = (∫_ℝ A⁺ dt).toReal − (∫_ℝ A⁻ dt).toReal = (∫_M |G| q⁺ dH^{n+1}).toReal − (∫_M |G| q⁻ dH^{n+1}).toReal. The last equality is (CF) for q⁺ and q⁻.
7. The function x ↦ |G(x)|q(x) is Borel and integrable for H^{n+1}⌞M, since ∫_M ||G|q| dH^{n+1} = ∫_M |G||q| dH^{n+1} < ∞. Because |G| ≥ 0, its positive and negative parts are |G|q⁺ and |G|q⁻ (ENNReal.ofReal(|G|q) = ENNReal.ofReal|G|·ENNReal.ofReal q, and likewise for −q). By integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part again, ∫_M |G| q dH^{n+1} = (∫_M |G| q⁺ dH^{n+1}).toReal − (∫_M |G| q⁻ dH^{n+1}).toReal.
8. Comparing steps 6 and 7 gives ∫_ℝ ∫_{S_t} q dHⁿ dt = ∫_M |G| q dH^{n+1}. This proves (3). ∎
proof_key_steps: (CF) for |q|, q⁺, q⁻ gives a.e.-measurable slice integrals A, A⁺, A⁻ with ∫A = ∫_M |G||q| < ∞.
A(t) < ∞ for a.e. t, so q is integrable on a.e. slice and F(t) = A⁺(t).toReal − A⁻(t).toReal there.
|F| ≤ A gives integrability of F on ℝ.
∫F = (∫A⁺).toReal − (∫A⁻).toReal = (∫_M|G|q⁺).toReal − (∫_M|G|q⁻).toReal = ∫_M |G|q.

subproblems.title: Basic calculus of integer multiplicity representations: locality of approximate tangent spaces, restriction, differences, orientation bound (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: (a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) if and only if M' does. (b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm).

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity triple carried by a Borel subset of a rectifiable set with tangent data (Simon Ch. 6, Definition 4.4)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and Hⁿ := μHE[n]. Let A ⊆ S ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel sets with S countably n-rectifiable; let θ : ℝ^P → ℕ be Borel with θ(x) > 0 for every x ∈ S and ∫_{S∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; and let ζ : ℝ^P → MultiVector P n (n-vectors, the continuous linear functionals on n-covectors) be a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞A. Assume that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A there is a linear subspace Q of ℝ^P such that S has approximate tangent space Q at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q) and ζ(x) is a unit orientation of Q (contract IsUnitOrientationOf). Then (A, θ, ζ) is an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P of dimension n: there is R : IMRep univ n with R.carrier = A, R.mult = θ and R.orient = ζ.

im_calculus (a) with U = ℝ^P, M = A, M' = S: a.e. on A, A and S have the same approximate tangent spaces.
So a.e. on A, A has approximate tangent space Q and ζ(x) is a unit orientation of Q.
Assemble the IMRep fields: Borel carrier, rectifiability by monotonicity, positive Borel multiplicity, local integrability by monotonicity, measurable orientation, orients.
